mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of the periods following a sustained decline in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals labor market weakness, which leads to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side, which boosts economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow by less than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates a weakening in consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in a single month, it signals a significant labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it indicates inflationary pressure coupled with high borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% signals strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods following a sustained increase in GDPC1.
